# Simulation: The Frog on the Lily Pads

## Question 1 (a) Code Comment

```{r}
#Define function named hop, while input is the initial position, setting up probability of going right as 0.5.
hop <- function(position, p_right = 0.5) {
  #Set up from going either -1 or 1, missing number of trials(size), defined probability going left as 1- 0.5.
  step <- sample(c(-1, 1), prob = c(p_right, 1 - p_right))
  #update the new position
  position + step
  #return function
  return(position)
}
#Testing with calling function hop with value 4 as initial
hop(4)

```

## Question 1 (b) Updating Code
```{r}
  #setting up initial position in the function
hop <- function(position = 4, p_right = 0.5) {
  #Picking random number from -1 or 1 for next direction, and probability of going right is 0.5, with left as 1-0.5=0.5
  step <- sample(c(-1, 1),
                 size =1, 
                 prob = c(1-p_right,p_right))
  #update the new position, name new position as new_position for better tracking
  new_position <- position+ step
  #return function
  return(new_position)
}

hop()
```

## Question 3(b) Repeated games CI Calculations
```{r 3bCI}
#finding 95% CI and Histogram
nbankr <- sum(results_Q3$banks == "right",na.rm = TRUE)
n_total <- length(results_Q3$banks)
p_right_bank <- nbankr/ n_total
#using binomial testing with nbankr as x and ntotal as y
ci<- binom.test(
  x = nbankr,
  n = n_total,
  conf.level = 0.95
)

lower_ci = ci$conf.int[1]
upper_ci = ci$conf.int[2]

c(p_right_bank = p_right_bank, lower_ci = lower_ci, upper_ci = upper_ci)
```

## Question 4(d) Add error bars to both plots, showing 95% confidence intervals for the proportions and standard errors for the mean numbers of hops.
```{r 4d}
#get CI values
lower_ci <- numeric(7)
upper_ci <- numeric(7)
#use the code of 3a again but loop it in 1-7
for (n in 1:7) {
  #finding 95% CI and Histogram
  nbankr <- sum(results_Q4[[n]]$banks == "right",na.rm = TRUE)
  n_total <- length(results_Q4[[n]]$banks)
  #using binomial testing with nbankr as x and ntotal as y
  ci<- binom.test(
    x = nbankr,
    n = n_total,
    conf.level = 0.95
  )
  
  lower_ci[n] = ci$conf.int[1]
  upper_ci[n] = ci$conf.int[2]

}
#plot graphs for proportions
plot_rb4b(results_Q4)
# Add 95% confidence interval error bars
arrows(
  x0 = 1:7,
  y0 = lower_ci,
  x1 = 1:7,
  y1 = upper_ci,
  angle = 90, code = 3, length = 0.05
)

#plot graphs for numbers of hops
#from 4(a) get values of mean hops and SD
mean_hops <- numeric(7)
sd_hops <- numeric(7)

for (n in 1:7){
  mean_hops[n]<-results_Q4[[n]]$frog_stats["mean_hops"]
  sd_hops[n]<- results_Q4[[n]]$frog_stats["sd_hops"]
}
#Calculate standard error for 1000 games
se_hops <- sd_hops / sqrt(1000)
#plot the graphs again
plot_rb4c(results_Q4)

# Add standard error bars
arrows(x0 = 1:7,
       y0 = mean_hops - se_hops,
       x1 = 1:7,
       y1 = mean_hops + se_hops,
       angle = 90,
       code = 3,
       length = 0.05)

```

## Question 5 A windy day
## 5(a) Report the proportion of games ending on the right bank (with a 95% confidence interval) and the mean and standard deviation of the number of hops for both games.
```{r 5a}
#Call Q3 equations with setting p_right to 0.7 as windy day
results_Q5 <- simulate_frogs(n_sims= 1000, p_right = 0.7)
#get comparison with fair day, and windy day
fair =results_Q3$frog_stats
windy =results_Q5$frog_stats

#set up function to compare ci for fair and windy
compare_ci <- list(results_Q3, results_Q5)
#set up vector for 2 ci
lower_ci <- numeric(2)
upper_ci <- numeric(2)
#loop through both cases
for (n in 1:2) {
  nbankr <- sum(compare_ci[[n]]$banks == "right", na.rm = TRUE)
  n_total <- length(compare_ci[[n]]$banks)

  ci <- binom.test(
    x = nbankr,
    n = n_total,
    conf.level = 0.95
  )

  lower_ci[n] <- ci$conf.int[1]
  upper_ci[n] <- ci$conf.int[2]
}
#return for values for comparison
fair
windy
# Display both ci of fair and windy
c(Fair_Lower = lower_ci[1],
  Fair_Upper = upper_ci[1],
  Windy_Lower = lower_ci[2],
  Windy_Upper = upper_ci[2])

```
